The `ValueError: No stream arrays were passed` was already right, but it arrived
with nothing to explain it. php prints two warnings first: it names the class
when that class defines no `stream_cast()` — `W::stream_cast is not
implemented!` — and then always reports `Cannot represent a stream of type
user-space as a select()able descriptor`.

The two are not one message with an optional half. A class that DOES define
`stream_cast()` and simply answers `false` gets only the second, which is what
